summary.en: Salvadoran forces have bombed gang leader Jeff's luxury mansion and destroyed the Mawozo headquarters, killing about 20 gang members, while Haitian security forces retook the national stadium after two years of gang control. Haiti formalised a security pact with El Salvador and deployed Salvadoran troops who have engaged in combat against gangs, prompting both supportive and oppositional street protests. The United Nations warned that anti-gang operations must prioritise civilian protection, and the EU imposed sanctions on four Haitian gangs for serious human rights violations. Martine Moise, widow of the assassinated former leader, has registered to contest the presidential election. The UCDP recorded 193 battle-related deaths in 2024.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske styrker har bombet gjenglederen Jeffs luksusvilla og ødelagt Mawozo-hovedkvarteret, og drept omtrent 20 gjengmedlemmer, mens haitiske sikkerhetsstyrker tok tilbake nasjonalstadion etter to år med gjengkontroll. Haiti formaliserte en sikkerhetspakt med El Salvador og satte inn salvadoranske tropper som har vært i kamp mot gjenger, noe som har ført til både støttende og motstandende gateprotester. FN advarte om at anti-gjeng-operasjoner må prioritere sivile, og EU innførte sanksjoner mot fire haitiske gjenger for alvorlige brudd på menneskerettighetene. Martine Moise, enke etter den myrdede tidligere lederen, har registrert seg for å stille til presidentvalget. UCDP registrerte 193 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
